verified_findings.title: The Settings popover's metronome and count-in rows stay live while a recording plays
verified_findings.whats_wrong: The shipped transport disables its metronome and count-in buttons for a backing track, because the backing-track synthesiser ignores both. The Settings popover edits the SAME two values a second time and never receives hasBackingTrack. The slider moves, the number changes, nothing is heard. The plan's own Global Constraints (line 129) already state the rule it then fails to wire.
verified_findings.proposed_fix: Pass the flag through to the popover and disable the metronome-volume and count-in-volume rows with the mixer's existing unavailable-reason pattern (TrackRowProps.mixUnavailable, plan lines 911-916).
verified_findings.why_it_works: It reuses a pattern the plan already built and a constant it already defines (RECORDING, lines 1072 and 3254), so the two editors of one value finally agree about when that value is editable.
verified_findings.evidence: SHIPPED CODE, web/app/play/TransportRow.tsx (master 85eedd14): :53 const UNAVAILABLE = 'not available while the file plays its own recording'; :126 disabled={disabled || hasBackingTrack} (toggle-metronome); :136 same (toggle-countin). PLAN: SettingsPopoverProps at lines 2189-2204 carries no equivalent. Rows exist via ApiValueKey (1212-1217), the inventory (1335) and the writer (2379).

verified_findings.title: The claim that the engine cannot serialise its settings is false, and it is the stated reason for hand-transcribing 71 defaults
verified_findings.whats_wrong: Settings has no INSTANCE toJson, which is true but misleading: alphaTab.model.JsonConverter.settingsToJsObject DOES serialise a Settings. The plan uses 'there is no toJson' as the reason an implementer must hand-transcribe 71 defaults - 20 of them colour and font strings - out of a browser console. That transcription is both unnecessary and a standing source of drift.
verified_findings.before: There is no `toJson` on `Settings`, so the defaults have to be read out of a browser console once and written into the module by hand.
verified_findings.after: `Settings` has no INSTANCE `toJson`, but `alphaTab.model.JsonConverter.settingsToJsObject(new Settings())` serialises the whole tree (1817 leaves, ~31 KB). Do NOT transcribe the defaults: ship them and assert them in a co-located test against what that converter reports for a fresh `Settings()`. Note two traps - the converter lives under `model`, not the (empty at runtime) `json` namespace; and colours come back as packed signed integers (-16777216), not `#000000` strings, so a test asserting colour strings must read `settings.display.resources.<key>.rgba` instead.
verified_findings.proposed_fix: Restate the claim accurately and replace the transcribe instruction with a co-located test asserting each shipped default against the converter.
verified_findings.why_it_works: It turns a one-off manual copy into a check that fails when the engine's defaults move under a version bump - which is exactly when a hand-transcribed table silently goes stale.
verified_findings.evidence: RAN in plain Node against the installed 1.8.4: new Settings().toJson === undefined; at.json keys = [] (the json barrel is EMPTY at runtime); at.model.JsonConverter.settingsToJsObject is a function; returned a Map with 1817 leaf keys, 6 colour leaves, 164 font leaves; settingsToJson length = 31821 bytes.
verified_findings.verified_how: RAN a Node probe against the real library

verified_findings.title: A mistyped enum option name wipes a correct value and survives a reload
verified_findings.whats_wrong: JsonHelper.parseEnum returns undefined for an unrecognised name (enumType[undefined]) and the serializers assign it straight through, returning true as though it were handled. Because the whole document is pushed on every edit, that undefined is re-applied for the rest of the session. It is worse than the queued claim said: it does not merely fail to apply, it CLOBBERS a previously-correct value, throws nothing, logs nothing, and survives a settingsToJsObject / jsObjectToSettings round-trip. Neither existing guard catches it - the storage merge compares string to string, and the row gate walks names, not values.
verified_findings.before: (no validation step exists between the stored JSON and the restore push)
verified_findings.after: Before the restore push, run every stored value through a validation helper: any value absent from its row's option list is dropped back to the shipped default. Run it on the stored document, not on each edit, so one bad key cannot poison the session.
verified_findings.proposed_fix: Add a validation helper called before the restore push in Task 6.
verified_findings.why_it_works: It closes the only path by which a bad value reaches the engine, and it does so at the one moment the whole document is known - unlike the per-edit guards, which each see only a single key.
verified_findings.evidence: RAN against real Settings: BEFORE display.layoutMode = 0 (Page). fillFromJson with the typo 'Horzontal' -> display.layoutMode = undefined. With 'Horizontal' -> 1. Also s3.staveProfile went from 1 (ScoreTab) to undefined on a typo - OLD VALUE KEPT? false. fillFromJson threw? no. Round-tripped bad settings: still undefined. Source: alphaTab.core.mjs:25045-25055 (parseEnum), :29566 (DisplaySettingsSerializer).
verified_findings.severity_note: Queued as P2. The measured behaviour - silent corruption of a good value that survives a reload - argues for P1. Flagged for the maintainer rather than silently re-graded.
verified_findings.verified_how: RAN a Node probe end-to-end through fillFromJson

verified_findings.title: The scoreLoaded subscription contributes nothing but a wrong first read
verified_findings.whats_wrong: readPlayer is subscribed to BOTH scoreLoaded and playerReady. At scoreLoaded, actualPlayerMode is still Disabled - _setupOrDestroyPlayer is its only writer and returns early when there is no score - so a normal page load momentarily reports 'playback is turned off', and a file swap momentarily reports the OUTGOING player. Because playerReady fires straight after (and re-fires repeatedly), it self-corrects within milliseconds. So this is a visible flicker of the Play tooltip and the loading bar, not a stuck state.
verified_findings.proposed_fix: Drop the scoreLoaded subscription (plan line 3500); playerReady plus the existing applySetting call at line 3504 already cover every case.
verified_findings.why_it_works: playerReady is the only event guaranteed to run after the player instance exists, so removing the earlier read removes the only source of the wrong value without losing any coverage.
verified_findings.evidence: PLAN lines 3494-3501. LIBRARY: :45349 _actualPlayerMode = PlayerMode.Disabled (initial); :48025-48030 _onScoreLoaded triggers the event BEFORE _setupOrDestroyPlayer; :46680-46710 that method is the only writer and returns early at :46684 with no score. Visible via noPlayerComing at 3519-3521 and the Play tooltip at 3524.
verified_findings.correction: The queued item said this read was 'still on scoreLoaded' and framed it as something lap 1 missed. git log -S shows the playerReady line was added in c195801d - the commit that CREATED Task 8 - not by any lap-1 commit. Task 8's read was born on both events.
verified_findings.verified_how: RAN grep + git log -S over the plan and the library

verified_findings.title: The by-eye gate can pass without touching a single sound-rebuilding row
verified_findings.whats_wrong: The gate asks for one row per SECTION across eight sections, over ~90 rows. Apply mode is a different axis from section: the Player section alone holds 27 rows across three sources, so 'one row in Player' can be an api row, and all fourteen midi rows go untested - exactly where a wrong apply hides.
verified_findings.before: Open each of the eight sections and change at least one row in each, watching the score.
verified_findings.after: Open each of the eight sections - Display > General, Colors, Fonts, Paddings, Notation, Player, Stylesheet, Export - and change at least one row in each, watching the score. Then, separately, change one row of EACH WAY OF TAKING EFFECT: one that redraws, one that is pushed without a redraw, one that rebuilds the sound (any of the fourteen Player rows that do), and one stylesheet row. Press both Export buttons and open the two files they download.
verified_findings.proposed_fix: Walk one row per way-of-taking-effect as well as per section, and name the eight sections inline.
verified_findings.why_it_works: It covers the axis a wrong `apply` actually lives on. The section walk alone cannot reach it, because sections and apply modes cut across each other.
verified_findings.evidence: RAN awk over lines 3737-3739 and the inventory at 1330-1339. Apply modes are three (line 1226: 'render' | 'settings' | 'midi'); the gate never names them.
verified_findings.correction: The queued item said the gate could also skip stylesheet rows. It cannot - Stylesheet IS one of the eight sections (line 1338, 12 rows). Only the 14 midi rows are skippable. Narrow the finding to that.
verified_findings.also_fixes: Task 10 Step 2 says 'the eight sections' without naming them; the enumeration only exists at line 3749.

verified_findings.area: Global Constraints + Task 4 Step 7 (the fourteen sound-rebuilding rows)
verified_findings.title: Fourteen rows stop the music and rewind it, contradicting the reason a popover was chosen
verified_findings.whats_wrong: Applying any of the fourteen midi rows calls loadMidiForScore, which calls AlphaSynth.loadMidiFile -> stop(). That pauses playback AND resets tickPosition to the start. The plan promises 'neither popover blocks the player', which is the single stated reason v0 chose a popover over a modal. The non-blocking e2e case uses the zoom row, which takes the redraw path, so the lane never exercises the path that breaks the claim.
verified_findings.after: Neither popover blocks the player on the redraw and push-only paths. The fourteen rows that rebuild the sound are the exception: `loadMidiForScore()` stops playback and rewinds to the start of the song (or the loop), so a change there is not something to make mid-take. Say so on the rows, and add an e2e case that plays, changes one sound-rebuilding row, and asserts the playhead moved to the start - the existing non-blocking case uses the zoom row, which never reaches this path.
verified_findings.proposed_fix: State the exception in the Global Constraints and in the funnel comment, scope the non-blocking promise to the redraw and push-only paths, and add a case that exercises a midi row while playing.
verified_findings.why_it_works: It makes the promise true as written, and it puts a test on the path that falsifies the broad version of the claim.
verified_findings.evidence: SOURCE: :46718 comment 'This will result in the player to stop playback'; :46722 loadMidiForScore; :40054 loadMidiFile -> :40055 this.stop(); :39987-39995 stop() pauses, stops the sequencer, noteOffAll, and sets tickPosition back to the range start. RAN a headless AlphaSynth with a stub output: after play() state = 1 (Playing), tickPosition 1921; after a 2nd loadMidiFile state = 0 (Paused), tickPosition = 1.
verified_findings.correction: 'Resets the synthesizer' OVERSTATES it - stop() calls noteOffAll(true), which ends active voices; soundfonts, presets and channel state survive. The damaging part is the rewind to tick 0, so it is not a pause you can resume from.
verified_findings.verified_how: RAN a live headless synth probe

verified_findings.title: Turning off the last drawn track does nothing and explains nothing
verified_findings.whats_wrong: applyRendered guards against emptying the drawn set by returning before api.renderTracks is ever called. It performs NO state update at all - the checkbox is fully controlled by renderedIndexes, which is written only from the renderFinished event. So with one track left, nothing fires, renderedIndexes never changes, and the control does not move by a single frame. Nothing is announced either.
verified_findings.proposed_fix: Give TrackRow a SECOND reason prop for the render lock and disable the control when it is the last drawn track.
verified_findings.why_it_works: A disabled control with a tooltip is the pattern the plan already built for the recording case, so the person gets the same affordance and the same explanation instead of a dead click.
verified_findings.evidence: PLAN lines 3167-3179 (applyRendered), 3305-3306 (the controlled prop), 3150-3152 (renderFinished is the only writer of renderedIndexes). Existing pattern at 911-916, the constant at 1072 and 3254, the disable rule at 1126, a VR story at 1157.
verified_findings.correction: Do NOT reuse mixUnavailable. Its own comment (lines 911-916) explicitly exempts render-select - 'Render-select, the display toggles and Transpose full stay live' - because those change the drawn score and keep working while a recording plays. The render lock needs its own prop.

verified_findings.title: A failed export leaves the button looking clicked and says nothing
verified_findings.whats_wrong: Neither export row has a try/catch or any success or failure signal. The Guitar Pro path builds bytes, creates a Blob, an object URL and a link, and clicks it - any of which can throw. The silent `if (!api?.score || !engine) return;` guard is a second quiet exit. The successful path needs nothing, because the browser's own download is the signal.
verified_findings.proposed_fix: Wrap both export actions in try/catch and raise a Sonner toast on failure only.
verified_findings.why_it_works: It matches the one other user-visible failure path the plan already has (the corrupt-stored-settings toast in Task 6), so a person gets told in the way this app already tells them.
verified_findings.evidence: PLAN lines 2385-2403 (runAction). RAN grep -ci toast -> 11 occurrences plan-wide; examples at 2788 and 2754.
verified_findings.correction: The queued item said 'every other failure path in this plan raises a toast'. That is generous - there is really ONE other user-visible failure path (Task 6's corrupt stored settings), plus line 134, which FORBIDS a toast on playerReady. Say 'the plan's only other user-visible failure path uses a toast'.
